_doc: Declared numeric range of every free identifier that reaches a CUDA grid axis.
This table is the HAND-MAINTAINED half of GenLaunch.v and it is an ASSUMPTION,
not a derivation. Whether n_tokens is a whole context or one prefill chunk is a
property of the Rust caller; no amount of CUDA parsing recovers it. What makes
the assumption safe to hold is that extract/launch_geometry.py REFUSES on any
identifier reaching an axis that is absent here -- so a new launcher cannot
quietly inherit someone else's bound.
lo/hi          the declared inclusive range. lo must be >= 0.
why            where the bound comes from, in words.
cite           file:line of the guard or config field, when there is one.
input_scaled   true when the bound is a property of the caller rather than of a
guard in the CUDA. Every input_scaled identifier that lands on
gridDim.y or .z gets a machine-checked _unlaunchable_at_ theorem
in GenLaunch.v showing where it breaks.
unenforced     what is MISSING: no assert, no clamp, no early return. These are
listed by the generator on every run. An `unenforced` note that the
guard scanner contradicts is reported beside the ENFORCED line, so
a note cannot outlive the gap it described.
Enforcement is NOT declared here: extract/launch_geometry.py reads guards out of the
host launcher's AST (early return, then-branch, else-branch) and accepts one only if
it bounds the same DECLARATION that reaches the axis, dominates the launch, and keeps
the axis inside the CUDA limit. Anything less stays a counterexample.
A key may be scoped 'rust/.../file.cu:ident', 'file.cu:ident' or bare 'ident';
the most specific wins. Every entry today is fully scoped on purpose: an
unscoped bound would let one file's 'N' silently license another file's.

Model constants cited above: config.json text_config: hidden_size=5376 intermediate_size=21504 num_attention_heads=32 num_key_value_heads=16 head_dim=256 global_head_dim=512 num_global_key_value_heads=4 vocab_size=262144 max_position_embeddings=262144

excluded_launches.why: vendored vLLM Marlin. The launched callee is a FUNCTION POINTER returned by get_marlin_kernel(...), a 14-argument dispatch over (a_type, b_type, c_type, s_type, thread_m_blocks, thread_n_blocks, thread_k_blocks, m_block_size_8, has_act_order, has_zp, group_blocks, num_threads, is_zp_float, stages). It does not resolve to a __global__ FunctionDecl, so there is no kernel to state an obligation about. This is the only launch in the corpus that is genuinely unanalyzable. The generator refuses if this entry ever stops matching, so the exclusion cannot outlive the code it excuses.
